I've found the bug. Let me trace through the logic to confirm.

At `tabulate/__init__.py:2369`, `_pad_row` is applied to every row including the reinserted `SEPARATING_LINE` (which is the bare string `"\001"`). When `padding > 0` (psql has `padding=1`), `_pad_row` iterates over the **characters** of the string `"\001"`, producing `[" \001 "]` — a list whose element has padding spaces around it. Then at line 2406, `_is_separating_line([" \001 "])` returns `False` because `" \001 " != "\001"`, so it renders as a data row.

With `padding=0` (e.g. `simple`), `pad=""` so the result is `["\001"]` and `row[0] == "\001"` still holds — which is why only padded tables break.

## Summary

The `SEPARATING_LINE` row was being rendered as an ordinary data row instead of a horizontal rule. Two related bugs in `tabulate/__init__.py`:

1. **`_pad_row` corrupted separating-line rows** (`_format_table`, line 2372): The reinserted `SEPARATING_LINE` is the bare string `"\001"`. When `fmt.padding > 0` (psql, grid, etc.), `_pad_row` iterated over the *characters* of that string, producing `[" \001 "]`. The padded element no longer equalled `"\001"`, so `_is_separating_line` returned `False` and it was rendered as a data cell. (With `padding=0` formats like `simple`, `pad=""` left it as `["\001"]`, which still matched — which is why only padded tables broke.) Fix: skip padding for separating-line rows.

2. **The `linebetweenrows` branch never handled separating lines** (line 2382): Formats like `grid`/`simple_grid`/`fancy_grid` took a branch that drew every row as a data row with no `_is_separating_line` check, so the sep line became an empty `||` data row. Fix: render sep lines as a single rule there, and skip the redundant line-between-rows when the next row is a separator (avoids duplicate rules).

3. **`rowaligns` length mismatch** (line 2219): `rowaligns` was built from `len(rows)` *before* `_reinsert_separating_lines` added the sep lines back, so `zip(padded_rows, rowaligns)` silently truncated and dropped trailing data rows. Fix: reinsert placeholder alignments at the same sep-line indices so `rowaligns` stays 1:1 with `padded_rows` (this also makes user-supplied per-row `rowalign` lists align correctly with their data rows when sep lines are present).

The fix is behavior-preserving for tables without separating lines (the new branches only add `_is_separating_line` handling), and now renders `SEPARATING_LINE` as a horizontal rule across every format (psql, grid, simple_grid, fancy_grid, heavy_grid, github, pipe, outline, simple, plain, etc.) and any column-type mix.
